title: Laboratory
intro: Laboratory stores the issuing laboratory name, address, contact details and logo used by report templates. It also sets the default facility register and the local time zone.

Use your real laboratory details and approved logo. The pictures show a fictional laboratory in a test installation. No practice data is required. You need View settings to open the page and Edit general settings to save it.
The issuing laboratory is the organisation producing reports. Facilities are the organisations sending work. Choosing a default register here does not create or import facilities.

tasks.title: Save your laboratory details
intro: Use this after installation or when the issuing laboratory details change.
steps: Open your user menu at the bottom left, choose Settings, then select Laboratory.
Enter your issuing laboratory name in Laboratory name. The example uses Documentation laboratory.
Enter the address for your letterhead in Address. It can contain more than one line.
Enter your approved contact details in Contact. The picture uses an example.invalid email address.
In Facility register, select an existing registered source. If the needed source is absent, register it through Facilities first. This choice supplies the default register for the Facility form.
Set the time zone when applicable

For PostgreSQL or MySQL, enter a named time zone such as Africa/Dar_es_Salaam. Read the help below the field. SQL Server requires a Windows time-zone name in each report run instead, so leave this setting empty there.
Open the page dots at the top right and select Save.
tasks.result: The saved details remain when you reopen Laboratory.

tasks.title: Remove an old logo
intro: Use this when the current logo should no longer appear in templates that use the laboratory logo.
steps: Select Clear beside Logo. This changes the draft only.
Open the page dots and select Save.
tasks.result: The saved laboratory settings no longer contain a logo.

tasks.title: Upload the laboratory logo
intro: Use a PNG or JPEG file up to 256 KB. Transparent PNG is useful for a letterhead logo.
steps: Select Choose file… beside Logo and select your approved local image.
Confirm that the expected image appears beside Logo. The picture reuses the test installation's shipped mark.
Open the page dots and select Save.
tasks.result: The logo remains after reopening Laboratory. A report template must use the laboratory tokens to display these values.

tasks.title: Change laboratory details on a phone
intro: Use the same fields on a phone. The page scrolls vertically.
steps: Enter the laboratory name and other fields within the phone-width form.
Scroll down to the logo preview and Choose file control. Save changes through the page dots.

end.title: Use the details in report templates
paragraphs: Report templates can use {{lab.name}}, {{lab.address}}, {{lab.contact}} and {{lab.logo}}. The page prints these token names below its description. Use Report Designer to place them in a template. Saving Laboratory does not edit a template.

end.title: Optional practice
paragraphs: In a test installation, save a fictional laboratory name and example.invalid contact address. Reuse an approved test PNG or JPEG for the upload exercise. Restore your intended settings afterward.

end.title: Limits
paragraphs: The logo accepts PNG and JPEG, up to 256 KB. SVG, WebP and image web addresses are not accepted. The register picker lists existing sources; it cannot register one.

end.title: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: The register list is empty. Open Facilities and register the source before returning here.
The time zone is refused. Use a named zone, not a fixed offset. Follow the SQL Server exception shown below the field.
The logo is refused. Check its format and size. Choose a PNG or JPEG no larger than 256 KB.
A report does not show the saved details. Check whether its template uses the laboratory tokens.

end.title: Related guides
paragraphs: Read Facilities to register a source. Read Setup checks to review readiness. Read Start here for command-line setup.
